D009-D011_h001.question_both:
It kind of feels like I live in two different gears, and neither one is really working for me.

For most of this past year, it’s like a cloud settled over everything. I used to be proud of clearing cases, but lately, even when we close a tough one, I just feel… nothing. My wife will say she’s proud, my lieutenant will compliment me, and I just nod. Inside, it’s like, “So what?” Getting through paperwork or even reading a report wears me out mentally in minutes; my brain feels like it’s slogging through mud. I’ve gotten so low at times that I actually sat in my car outside the pharmacy, thinking about buying a bunch of pills and just ending it. I’ve even stashed a bottle at home “just in case.”

But then, about a month ago, it flipped. I’ve been wound up, snapping at people over tiny things—a typo in a report, someone chewing too loud. I can’t sit still in briefings; I’m pacing the back of the room, drumming my fingers. I’m talking nonstop—my partner jokes he can’t get a word in—and I’ve got this restless energy, like I need to be moving, doing something. I barely sleep, maybe a couple hours, and I don’t even feel tired.

There’s this constant edge of nervousness under it all—like I’m always bracing for something—but I can’t tell if that’s from the job, from my mood, or both. My work has definitely taken a hit during the low parts; I’ve been slower, missing small details, and my supervisor’s noticed. At home, my wife says she doesn’t know which version of me she’s coming home to anymore.

I couldn’t sit still; on breaks I’d be pacing, finding extra tasks, asking for more shifts, trying to start side projects after work. I’d sleep maybe 2–3 hours, sometimes none, and feel like I didn’t need it. My head would race with ideas and I’d talk nonstop, like I couldn’t shut up or tolerate silence. Lately I’ve been having very specific thoughts about not wanting to be here anymore. I’ve thought through how and where I’d do it, in a way that scares me when I step back.

What’s confusing is that about a year ago, for roughly a month, I was the opposite. I was snapping at colleagues over tiny things, pacing the ward on my breaks, unable to sit still. I slept maybe three hours a night but felt oddly energized, talking nonstop in meetings. My mind was racing with ideas and impulses that weren’t really about worry; they just came, fast and relentless. I’d be jumping from one thing to another, very keyed into every little noise in the hallway or bird at the window. I’ve been taking on extra projects—new papers, new course ideas, reorganizing the whole syllabus system—often all at once. I sleep maybe four or five hours a night, but I wake up feeling strangely energized, not like when I’m normally tired.

At the same time, my mind feels keyed up a lot. I worry about my students, my job security, whether I’m being a good partner. I’m not sure if the restlessness and doing so much come from that worry or if it’s something separate; it all kind of blurs together.
